text:
Jordan: Heads up — quick design check on notify preview sequencing. In compact preview, toggling 'primary channel' seems to swap order but visually it's confusing on mobile. Screenshot attached.
Priya: oh yeah, saw that. When you toggle the switch the preview animation reorders channels without aria-live update. Screen reader users won't get context. :grimacing:
Sam: Agree. Two issues: (1) visual flip is abrupt, (2) the suppressed-channel pill color fails contrast ratio at 14px. I ran it through Axe. /screenshot
Marta: Proposed copy tweak: change 'Suppress notifications' -> 'Quiet period' ? Thoughts?
Jordan: Quiet period feels better. Also thinking the toggle should be select-style so order doesn't shift — instead show 'Primary' badge. That avoids animation.
Priya: Select-style is better for accessibility. We can also add aria-live='polite' on the preview list to announce changes. @Sam can you confirm copy length for mobile?
Sam: Yep. 'Quiet period' fits. For small screens we should truncate channel names but reveal full name on hover/focus. Also increase suppressed-pill contrast to #1F2937 on light theme (meets 4.5:1).
Jordan: Nice. Also request: when primary is offline fallback should show inline reason 'No device' — need consistent affordance for fallback vs explicit routing.
Marta: Copy nit: 'Send to backup' -> 'Fallback channel' — clearer for non-ops users.
Priya: I'll update Figma. Quick prototype Q: do we keep reorder animation for desktop only? Maybe reduced motion preference should disable it too. :white_check_mark:
Sam: Code note: current behavior implemented in notifyPreview.jsx around the reorder handler. Quick patch: when prefers-reduced-motion detect, toggle class to instant swap. I'll open PR.
Jordan: SG. @preview-bot can we capture a11y checklist for this release?
preview-bot: preview-bot: Created checklist ticket: #PRJ-4321 — includes contrast, aria-live, reduced-motion, screenreader text, truncated tooltip.
Marta: :thumbsup: I'll drop updated copy in Figma by EOD. Sam please link PR when ready.
